name: clanker
blurb: A jokey Star Wars insult for robots and AI that went viral on TikTok in 2025
title: Clanker Meaning: The Star Wars Insult for Robots and AI
description: Clanker is a mocking word for robots and AI. It comes from Star Wars, where clone troopers call battle droids clankers, and spread on TikTok in mid-2025.
answer: Clanker is a mocking insult for robots and AI, from chatbots to delivery robots. It comes from Star Wars: clone troopers call battle droids "clankers" in the 2005 game Star Wars: Republic Commando and in the animated series The Clone Wars. In late June 2025 a TikTok of someone yelling "clanker" at a delivery robot went viral, and the word spread as a jokey way to vent about AI.

body: The name imitates the clanking sound metal droids make when they move. It first appeared in Republic Commando (2005) and was used in the first episode of Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008). Prequel-meme communities kept it alive for years before it broke out in 2025.

Its sudden popularity matched a wider mood: robots and AI tools were showing up everywhere, from customer service to food delivery, and people wanted a funny word to push back. Dictionary.com put clanker on its 2025 Word of the Year shortlist, and Merriam-Webster and Collins later added it.

The word appears in the first episode of Star Wars: The Clone Wars.
A TikTok of someone calling a delivery robot a clanker goes viral; the word spreads as a general insult for AI.
Skits imagining a future where humans and robots live together rack up millions of views.
Dictionary.com lists clanker on its Word of the Year 2025 shortlist.
Merriam-Webster (January) and Collins (April) publish entries for the word.

ul: To a chatbot that gets something wrong: "Wrong again, clanker."
At a self-checkout that keeps beeping: "This clanker hates me."
Skits: a dad meeting his daughter's robot boyfriend, "No clanker is coming to Sunday dinner."
Mock apology: "I'm sorry for every time I said clanker, please spare me in the robot uprising."

sections.h: Tone and is it still popular?
body: Clanker is meant as a joke: the target is a machine, and much of the humour is how seriously people pretend to take it. Still, some linguists and critics noted that certain skits borrowed the patterns of real-world discrimination, so it is worth keeping the jokes about the machines themselves. The word peaked in summer 2025 and is now an everyday, slightly dated way to grumble about AI, alongside other words like "slop" for low-quality AI content.

faq.a: Star Wars. Clone troopers use it for battle droids in the 2005 game Republic Commando and in The Clone Wars TV series.
It is an insult aimed at machines, used jokingly. People call it a "robot slur" as part of the joke; it is not used against people.

faq.q: Why did clanker go viral in 2025?
faq.a: A viral TikTok of someone yelling it at a delivery robot in June 2025, plus wide frustration with AI showing up everywhere.
